stories.title: A tri-modular feline infectious peritonitis virus nanoparticle vaccine confers complete protection in female cats without detectable antibody-dependent enhancement
stories.description: Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) complicates coronavirus vaccine development. Feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV) is a classic model of coronavirus vaccine-mediated ADE. Here, we develop ferritin-based FIPV nanoparticle vaccines displaying nucleocapsid (N) antigen, antigen-presenting cell (APC)-targeting ligands, and immunostimulatory factors, and evaluate their protective efficacy, serum-mediated ADE risk, and associated immune features. Compared with soluble N protein, the single-module FIPV N nanoparticle vaccine (sfNnps) enhances FIPV N-specific T-cell responses yet confers only 25.0% (2/8) protection. Dual-module vaccines incorporating either the APC-targeting ligand HCV E2 (dfN/Hnps) or the immunostimulatory factor IFNγ (dfN/Inps) further boost N-specific T-cell responses and confer 50.0% (4/8) and 62.5% (5/8) protection, respectively. The tri-modular vaccine co-displaying N, HCV E2, and IFNγ (tfN/HInps) elicits the most robust N-specific T-cell responses and affords 100% (8/8) protection in female cats, while showing no detectable serum-mediated ADE under the tested conditions and reducing peripheral-blood viral RNA levels by 73.0%. Immune profiling associates tfN/HInps with increased cDC1 representation and antigen-presentation gene expression, as well as a shift toward CD8⁺ effector-memory T cells and a FOXO1-centered program linked to transcriptional features of increased proliferation, memory formation, and cytotoxicity. Overall, this engineered FIPV nano‑display vaccine could provide a framework for cellular‑immunity‑oriented vaccine development against ADE‑prone coronaviruses. This study shows that a tri-modular ferritin nanoparticle vaccine against feline infectious peritonitis virus elicits strong cellular immunity and provides protection in female cats without detectable serum-mediated antibody-dependent enhancement.

stories.title: A double debris disc around a white dwarf sculpted by two planetary bodies
stories.description: Many planetary systems survive the metamorphosis of their host stars into white dwarfs, as demonstrated by the detection of dusty circumstellar discs around these stellar remnants and chemical signatures of planetary debris in atmospheres of these stars. A small fraction of these circumstellar discs also contain gas, detected in the form of emission lines from various ionic transitions (most commonly the near-infrared Ca II triplet). All of the 21 known gas discs exhibit double-peaked line profiles characteristic of a rotating flat disc. The mechanism behind the generation of gas is still debated, but for at least one system it has been linked with the presence of a surviving planetesimal embedded within the dust disc. Here we report the discovery of WD J132800.85–145019.95, a new gas-disc system that exhibits quadruple-peaked instead of double-peaked line profiles. These emission lines originate from two separate gaseous rings extending from 0.14 R⊙ to 0.34 R⊙ and from 0.54 R⊙ to 1.93 R⊙. We propose that this structure results from the presence of two distinct planetary bodies within these discs, ranging in size from a few kilometres to the size of Pluto. The detection this stable double-disc presents a new challenge for the current models of debris disc formation and evolution. Scientists discovered a white dwarf star circled by two nested rings of gas that were probably shaped by two hidden planetary bodies, one asteroid-sized and one Pluto-sized. The star’s unusual four-peaked light signature reveals a striking new kind of planetary debris system.
